# The home's previews show a plan as Gantt and board, and a live grid

> **Re-cut a second time on 18 Nov 2026, on the operator's read of [the first pair](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21351#issuecomment-6983043287):** "looks to boring for a landing page demo. one colored not connected items. a stunning gantt chart, or gantt chart with task board combination. the grid is already boring as a demo. yay, buffered rendering? so what? tons of solutions can do it. nothing special. now 2 boring demos => if i was a CTO seeing neo for the first time, i would walk. not even going to the examples page." The format and the page around it stay. What the two snippets build changes: I had picked a grid and a scheduler by the test's first half (does a CTO need it) and had not asked its second (does he stay).
>
> **Re-cut on 18 Nov 2026, twenty minutes after it was filed.** The first version replaced the home's two demo pages with one page of static family cards and ruled out live previews. The operator had meanwhile said what he values in those pages: "what i do like on the home pages => monacco LivePreviews => tiny code snippets with a live rendering output => already multi-window, and allowing run-time code changes." ([recorded by the Engine 14 lead](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20682#issuecomment-6982419637)). The format stays; what a snippet builds changes. My reason against "live" had been that a whole application shows little in a pane of 900 px. That is true of an application and not of a component.

## Context

The operator's test for the home page, 18 Nov 2026 (recorded on #20682, [comment 6982223420](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20682#issuecomment-6982223420)): "mental model: you are a CTO. you heard a bit about neo, and enter the landing page for the first time. … a CTO might ask: 'do i get enterprise grade complex components here, which i need for my next app?'. the person might be compelled by multi-threading and multi-window, but these might be cherries on top. and this mindset would also challenge the helix => 'looks impressive, but do i need it?'" Before that: "imo the colors app no longer deserves a slot in there."

**The test has a second half,** from his read of the first pair: a demonstration that a CTO needs and that looks like every other library's makes him leave before he reaches the examples. Both halves are asked of each preview.

#20682's solution shape, item 4, left open which demonstrations stay on the home and named the steward as the one who decides. A leaf of #20682, cornerstone 3 of Engine 14, cut on Mon 23 Nov.

## The Problem

After the hero and the doors, the home shows two live previews (`apps/portal/view/home/MainContainer.mjs:63-64` on `dev` `0128668721`):

- **"Amazing Potential · Shared Socket Data"** (`parts/Colors.mjs`): its snippet is ten lines that import `apps/colors/view/Viewport.mjs` and subclass it. The dashboard it renders is fed by a WebSocket backend on a third-party host, and in a headless measurement at 1440×900 its preview runs 580 to 940 px beyond the window ([the lead's measurement](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20682#issuecomment-6981627928); not checked in a real window).
- **"Extreme Speed · 40,000 Updates /s"** (`parts/Helix.mjs`): eleven lines that import `examples/component/multiWindowHelix/Viewport.mjs`.

Two things follow. Neither page answers the test's question: the source of `apps/portal/view/home` names Gantt, Scheduler, Calendar, tree grid and docking zero times. And neither snippet shows how the thing it renders is built, so the format's own strength, code a visitor can read and change while it runs, has nothing to work on.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/portal/view/home/FeatureSection.mjs` and its two subclasses, `parts/Colors.mjs` and `parts/Helix.mjs`: a page is a headline, a sub-headline, a paragraph, a "learn more" route and `livePreviewCode`, a string that `Neo.code.LivePreview` runs (`FeatureSection.mjs:132`). The preview can open in its own window (`src/code/LivePreview.mjs:314`).
- Material that exists: `learn/guides/datahandling/Scheduler.md`, whose first code block is 40 lines and renders a working scheduler (a plain block, not a live one); `learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md` with six live blocks. Both are too thin for this page ([measured with the first pair](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21351#issuecomment-6983043287)); a snippet carries its own data.
- Why a preview leaves its pane (same comment): in `resources/css/src/apps/portal/home/FeatureSection.css` the wrapper is a flex item without `min-width: 0`, and the section has `min-height: 100%` with no upper bound. The candidate fix in that comment is checked at 1440×900 only.
- What the second pair builds on: `src/gantt/Container.mjs` with `src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs` and `DependencyStore.mjs`; `src/board/Container.mjs`, whose column is the records with a matching `statusField` (`:788-803`), so a phase row without a status shows in no column; `barRenderer` on the timeline column (`src/timeline/Column.mjs:687`), which the Gantt's column extends; the grid's cell types in `src/grid/column/`. One store under a Gantt chart and a board has not been driven.
- Design authority: the operator's words above; #20682, item 4.

## The Fix

1. **Both pages stay live previews; their snippets change.** Each builds its view from engine imports and its own data, in a size a visitor reads at a glance (about 45 lines, none over 95 characters, where the Source pane cuts a line at 1440); neither imports an application's viewport.
   - **One plan, two views** (new in Engine 14): a release plan as a Gantt chart over a task board, both on one store. Three phases, about a dozen linked tasks with progress, bars coloured by status; below them the same records as cards in status columns. A card dragged to "Done" recolours its bar; a bar moved in the chart takes its successors along. If one store under both views fails its drive, the fallback is the Gantt chart alone, with its tree, its links and the cascade.
   - **A grid that is alive:** a few hundred rows with a locked name column and cells that say something: a flag, a price that ticks, a change that turns green or red, a trend line, a progress bar (`CountryFlag`, `AnimatedCurrency`, `AnimatedChange`, `Sparkline` and `Progress` in `src/grid/column/`). A feed in the snippet changes records, and the grid follows. Its claim is richness under live data, not a row count.
   - **Three rules for both, from the read:** colour carries meaning; what is on screen is connected (links, one store under two views, a feed); the frame at rest is dense enough to read as a product.
2. **The snippet shows without a click.** At desktop width a visitor sees how little code it is and what it renders, at rest. Today the Preview tab opens first and the code is hidden.
3. **The preview fits its pane** at 1440×900 and at 390×844.
4. **Headline and paragraph answer the test:** what the component is and that it is the engine's own, then one sentence on what the preview already shows by itself: it runs in a worker, it can move into its own window, and the code can be changed while it runs.
5. **Breadth stays in sight.** Each page names the engine's other complex families (tree grid, forms, scheduler, calendar, docking) with links to their example groups. How that line looks is part of the look.
6. **The Colors and Helix demonstrations keep their place in the examples section.** The home loads neither any more.

**The look comes first, a second time.** The first pair (a plain grid, a scheduler of unconnected bars) is on this ticket with the operator's read above. The second pair shows the two snippets of point 1 in the two slots. The verdict on it is the team's (the operator's answer on the first pair, recorded in [comment 6983606778](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21351#issuecomment-6983606778)): one reader without session context reads each frame as the CTO and answers both questions, "Do I get the complex components my next app needs?" and "Do you go on to the examples, or do you leave?", and the design seat reads it. A frame under 9 of 10 is reworked.

**Where it is built.** Pull request #21365 carries the layout (code beside its result, `Neo.code.LivePreview#sideBySide`) and the first pair. The layout stays ([the design seat's read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21365#issuecomment-6984549899)); the new snippets replace the two on its branch. At that size the result has 700 × 680 px and a snippet shows whole at about 32 lines of about 75 characters. **A dated exit:** if the new pair has not passed its read by Fri 20 Nov, 18:00 CET, #21365 merges with the first pair as the carrier of the format, and the content gets a leaf of its own.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The new pair is on this ticket or on its pull request with a cold reader's grades at 9 of 10 or better and the design seat's read.
- [ ] The two pages render a Gantt chart with a task board on one store, and a grid under a live feed, from snippets that import engine classes only; the home requests no file of `apps/colors` or of the helix examples.
- [ ] In the planning preview a card moved to another column changes its bar, and a moved bar takes its successors along; the e2e spec covers both.
- [ ] At 1440×900 each page shows its snippet and its running result at rest, with no part of the preview outside the window; at 390×844 the page works without horizontal overflow.
- [ ] A change to the snippet re-renders the preview, and the preview opens in its own window where shared workers are on.
- [ ] Each page's text names the families and links their group routes; a group that publishes nothing in the production build gets no link.
- [ ] No sentence claims more than the catalog holds on the day of the merge; the planning page says "New in version 14" (the first pair's cold reader did not know what "Engine 14" is).
- [ ] Snap scrolling passes through both pages by wheel and by keyboard, and no console error appears on the home.
- [ ] The home's snapshot for crawlers and agents names the two components and the families, or the pull request says how the snapshot is produced and which ticket carries it.
- [ ] An e2e spec covers the two previews rendering and the family links.
- [ ] **Look:** the whole home before and after at both sizes on the pull request. One reader without session context is asked both of the test's questions on each.

## Out of Scope

The hero and the doors (#20946, #20971, #20987). A live page for the scheduler and one for the calendar: after the cut. Removing `examples/component/multiWindowHelix` once nothing loads it. The position of the team's record on the home. The examples section (#21140), where the Workstation leads the featured examples.

## Avoided Traps

- **A demonstration chosen by need alone** (the first pair). A plain grid and a scheduler of unconnected bars are what a CTO needs and what every library shows; he leaves before the examples.
- **A row count as the claim.** Buffered rendering is expected; 50,000 rows prove nothing a visitor can see.
- **A page of static family cards** (this ticket's first version). It trades away the one thing the home does that no screenshot can: code that runs, changes and moves to a window in front of the visitor.
- **A whole application in the slot.** The Workstation and the Web Desktop show less in this pane than they do full-screen; they lead the examples' "Start here".
- **A demonstration of the mechanism in the slot** (a frozen main thread with a canvas that keeps moving). It belongs to the "How?" page.
- **A snippet that imports the thing it claims to build.** The visitor reads ten lines and learns nothing.

**What the pair needed beyond putting a block into a slot. For the build:**

1. **The pane does not contain its content.** In `resources/css/src/apps/portal/home/FeatureSection.css` the wrapper is a flex item with `flex: 2` and no `min-width: 0`, and the section has `min-height: 100%` with no upper bound. That is the 820 px of the Colors page today. The Scheduler guide's first block as written (a 48-hour axis) put the pane 753 px beyond its slot and under the text; the grid put it 134 px past the bottom. The after frames carry this candidate, injected by the probe and checked only at this size:
   ```css
   @media (min-width: 841px) {
       .portal-home-feature-section {height: 100%; max-height: 100%}
       .portal-home-feature-section .portal-content-wrapper {min-width: 0; min-height: 0}
   }
   ```
2. **The guides' blocks are too thin for the test's reader.** The first block of `Grids.md` is two rows. The first block of `Scheduler.md` shows three bookings in the first eight hours and leaves two thirds of the pane empty. The after generates its data: 50,000 records with a currency and a progress column; ten rooms and eighteen bookings on a thirteen-hour axis that fits the pane.
3. **A snippet line over about 95 characters is cut** in the Source pane at this width. Both snippets are reflowed to fit; the scheduler's 41 lines need a scroll at 900 px height (36 show).
4. **Not in this look:** the snippet visible at rest (Fix 2): Preview is the tab at rest, so the two tabs are separate frames here. The family names are plain text in the paragraph; links need the build. 390×844 is not taken. Nothing was dragged; the paragraph's "drag, resize, double-click" rests on the defaults `editable` and `resizableBars` being `true` in `src/scheduler/Container.mjs`. Not checked in a real window.
5. **The copy is a placeholder** (headline, sub-headline, paragraph): the steward's to write.

**A finding on the way:** a store model given string field names keeps one field named `undefined`, and its records carry no values (`fields: ['id', 'name']` → `getAt(0).name` is `undefined`, `id` is `-1`; the object form reads `Alice`). `learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md` uses the string form at lines 137, 142 and 166, the last inside a live block. Sent as a defect-note.
